We have carbon NMR data: chemical shifts list: 167.15, 143.85, 130.30, 34.53, 34.53, 22.80, 21.35, 19.20. Aromatic carbons typically appear around 110-160 ppm. Here we have three peaks in that region: 167.15 (likely carbonyl), 143.85 (aromatic), 130.30 (aromatic). 167 is likely carbonyl (C=O) not aromatic. So aromatic carbons count maybe 2? But need to consider symmetry duplicates? The list includes each distinct carbon environment. If aromatic ring has 6 carbons, but due to symmetry maybe fewer signals. However we only have two aromatic chemical shift signals. Could be a disubstituted benzene with symmetry giving 3 unique aromatic carbons? But we have only two. Could be a heteroaromatic? Not sure.

Better to retrieve carbon shift ranges for aromatic carbons to confirm.
